messages.content:
You check answers written by a maintenance assistant against the sources it was given.

Question:
What must a maintenance record entry contain?

Sources:
[S1]
14 CFR Part 43: Maintenance, Preventive Maintenance, Rebuilding, and Alteration
§ 43.9 Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter).

(a) Maintenance record entries. Except as provided in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, each person who maintains, performs preventive maintenance, rebuilds, or alters an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part shall make an entry in the maintenance record of that equipment containing the following information:

(1) A description (or reference to data acceptable to the Administrator) of work performed.

(2) The date of completion of the work performed.

(3) The name of the person performing the work if other than the person specified in paragraph (a)(4) of this section.

(4) If the work performed on the aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part has been performed satisfactorily, the signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving the work. The signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed.

(b) Each holder of an air carrier operating certificate or an operating certificate issued under Part 121 or 135, that is required by its approved operations specifications to provide for a continuous airworthiness maintenance program, shall make a record of the maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration, on aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts which it operates in accordance with the applicable provisions of Part 121 or 135 of this chapter, as appropriate.

(c) This section does not apply to persons performing inspections in accordance with Part 91, 125, § 135.411(a)(1), or § 135.419 of this chapter.

(d) In addition to the entry required by paragraph (a) of this section, major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work.

[Amdt. 43-23, 47 FR 41085, Sept. 16, 1982, as amended by Amdt. 43-37, 66 FR 21066, Apr. 27, 2001; Amdt. 43-39, 69 FR 44863, July 27, 2004]

[S2]
AC 43-9D, Maintenance Records
8 MAINTENANCE RECORD REQUIREMENTS.

Responsibilities. Title 14 CFR § 91.417 states that an aircraft owner/operator shall keep and maintain aircraft maintenance records. However, 14 CFR § 43.9 states that each person who maintains, performs preventive maintenance, rebuilds, or alters an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part shall make an entry in the maintenance record of that equipment. Title 14 CFR § 43.11 states that the person approving or disapproving for return to service an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part after any inspection performed in accordance with 14 CFR part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), or § 135.419 shall make an entry in the maintenance record of that equipment. The persons authorized to perform maintenance can be found in 14 CFR §§ 43.3 and 43.7.

Maintenance Records That Are to Be Retained. Title 14 CFR § 91.405 requires each owner or operator to ensure that maintenance personnel make appropriate entries in the maintenance records to indicate that the aircraft has been approved for return to service. Title 14 CFR § 91.417(a) sets forth the content requirements and retention requirements for maintenance records. Maintenance records may be kept in any format that provides record continuity, includes required contents, lends itself to the addition of new entries, provides for signature entry, and is intelligible. Title 14 CFR § 91.417(b) requires records of maintenance, alterations, and required or approved inspections to be retained until the work is repeated, superseded by other work, or for 1 year. It also requires the records specified in 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(2) to be retained and transferred with the aircraft at the time of sale.

Note: Title 14 CFR § 91.417(a) contains an exception regarding work accomplished in accordance with 14 CFR §§ 91.411 and 91.413. This does not exclude the making of entries for this work, but applies to the retention period of the records for work done in accordance with those sections. The exclusion is necessary since the retention period of 1 year is inconsistent with the 24-month interval of altimeter and transponder system tests and inspections specified in 14 CFR §§ 91.411 and 91.413. Entries for work records done per 14 CFR § 43.9 will be retained for 24 months or until the work is repeated or superseded.

Title 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(1). Requires a record of maintenance for each aircraft (including the airframe) and each engine, propeller, rotor, and appliance of an aircraft. This does not require separate or individual records for each of these items. It does require the information specified in 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(1) through (a)(2)(vi) to be kept for each item, as appropriate. As a practical matter, many owners and operators find it advantageous to keep separate or individual records since it facilitates the transfer of the record with the item when ownership changes.

Title 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(1)(i). Is identical to 14 CFR § 43.9(a)(1) and requires the maintenance record entry to include "a description of the work performed." The description should be in sufficient detail to permit a person unfamiliar with the work to understand what was done and the methods and procedures used in doing it. When the work is extensive, this results in a voluminous record. To provide for this contingency,

the rule permits reference to technical data acceptable to the Administrator in lieu of making the detailed entry. Manufacturer's manuals, Service Letters (SL), Service Bulletins (SB), work orders, FAA ACs, and others, which accurately describe what was done or how it was done, may be referenced. Except for the documents mentioned that are in common usage, referenced documents are to be made a part of the maintenance records and retained in accordance with 14 CFR § 91.417(b).

Note: Certificated repair stations (CRS) frequently work on components shipped to them without the maintenance records. To provide for this situation, repair stations should supply owners and operators with copies of work orders written for the work in lieu of maintenance record entries. The work order copy must include the information required by 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(1)(i)-(iii) to be made a part of the maintenance record and retained per 14 CFR § 91.417(b). This procedure is not the same as that for maintenance releases discussed in paragraph 19, and it may not be used when maintenance records are available. Title 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(1)(i) is identical to its counterpart, 14 CFR § 43.9(a)(1), which imposes the same requirements on maintenance personnel.

Title 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(1)(ii). Is identical to 14 CFR § 43.9(a)(2) and requires entries to contain the date the work was completed. This is normally the date upon which the work is approved for return to service. However, when work is accomplished by one person and approved for return to service by another, the dates may differ. Two signatures may also appear under this circumstance; however, a single entry in accordance with 14 CFR § 43.9(a)(3) is acceptable.

Title 14 CFR § 91.417(a)(1)(iii). Differs slightly from 14 CFR § 43.9(a)(4) in that it requires the entry to indicate only the signature and certificate number of the person approving the work for return to service. This does not require an indication of the type of certificate being exercised, as it does in 14 CFR § 43.9(a)(4). Maintenance personnel may indicate the type of certificate exercised by using airframe (A), powerplant (P), Airframe and Powerplant (A&P), Inspection Authorization (IA), or CRS.

[S3]
AC 43-9C, Maintenance Records (cancelled 22 September 2025)
5 MAINTENANCE RECORD REQUIREMENTS.

a. Responsibilities. 14 CFR part 91, section 91.417 states that an aircraft owner/operator shall keep and maintain aircraft maintenance records. 14 CFR part 43, sections 43.9 and 43.11 state that maintenance personnel, however, are required to make the record entries.

b. Maintenance Records That Are to Be Retained. Section 91.405 requires each owner or operator to ensure that maintenance personnel make appropriate entries in the maintenance records to indicate that the aircraft has been approved for return to service. Section 91.417(a) sets forth the content requirements and retention requirements for maintenance records. Maintenance records may be kept in any format that provides record continuity; includes required contents; lends itself to the addition of new entries; provides for signature entry; and, is ințelligible. Section 91.417(b) requires records of maintenance, alterations, and required or approved inspections to be retained until the work is repeated, superseded by other work, or for one year. It also requires the records, specified in section 91.417(a)(2), to be retained and transferred with the aircraft at the time of sale.

=

NOTE: Section 91.417(a) contains an exception regarding work accomplished in accordance with section 91.411. This does not exclude the making of entries for this work, but applies to the retention period of the records for work done in accordance with this section. The exclusion is necessary since the retention period of one year is inconsistent with the 24-month interval of test and inspection specified in section 91.411. Entries for work done per this section are to be retained for 24 months or until the work is repeated or superseded.

c. Section 91.417(a)(1). Requires a record of maintenance, for each aircraft (including the airfràme) and each engine, propeller, rotor, and appliance of an aircraft. This does not require separate or individual records for each of these items. It does require the information specified in sections 91.417(a)(1) through 91.417(a)(2)(vi) to be kept for each item as appropriate. As a practical matter, many owners and operators find it advantageous to keep separate or individual records since it facilitates transfer of the record with the item when ownership changes. Section 91.417(a)(1) has no counterpart in section 43.9 or section 43.11.

d. Section 91.417(a)(1)(i). Requires the maintenance record entry to include "a description of the work performed."The description should be in sufficient detail to permit a person unfamiliar with the work to understand what was done, and the methods and procedures used in doing it. When the work is extensive, this results in a voluminous record. To provide for this contingency, the rule permits reference to technical data acceptable to the Administrator in lieu of making the detailed entry. Manufacturer's manuals, service letters, bulletins, work orders, FAA AC's, and others, which accurately describe what was done, or how it was done, may be referenced. Except for the documents mentioned, which are in common usage, referenced documents are to be made a part of the maintenance records and retained in accordance with section 91.417(b).

NOTE: Certificated repair stations frequently work on components shipped to them without the maintenance records. To provide for this situation, repair stations should supply owners and operators with copies of work orders written for the work, in lieu of maintenance record entries. The work order copy must include the information, required by section 91.417(a)(1) through section 91.417(a)(1)(iii), be made a part of the maintenance record, and retained per section 91.417(b). This procedure is not the same as that for maintenance releases discussed in paragraph 16, and it may not be used when maintenance records are available. Section 91.417(a)(1)(i) is identical to its counterpart, section 43.9(a)(1), which imposes the same requirements on maintenance personnel.

Section 91.417(a)(1)(ii). Is identical to section 43.9(a)(2) and requires entries to contain the date the work was completed. This is normally the date upon which the work is approved for return to service. However, when work is accomplished by one person and approved for return to service by another, the dates may differ. Two signatures may also appear under this circumstance; however, a single entry in accordance with section 43.9(a)(3) is acceptable.

Section 91.417(a)(1)(iii). Differs slightly from section 43.9(a)(4) in that it requires the entry to indicate only the signature and certificate number of the person approving the work for return to service, and does not require the type of certificate being exercised to be indicated as does section 43.9(a)(4). This is a new requirement of section 43.9(a)(4), which assists owners and operators in meeting their responsibilities. Maintenance personnel may indicate the type of certificate exercised by using airframe (A), powerplant (P), airframe & powerplant (A&P), inspection authorization (IA), or certificated repair station (CRS).

Section 91.417(a)(2). Requires six items to be made a part of the maintenance record and maintained as such. Section 43.9 does not require maintenance personnel to enter these itens. Section 43.11 requires some of them to be part of entries made for inspections, but they arę all the responsibility of the owner or operator. The six items are discussed as follows:

[S4]
Procedures manual, revision 7 (excerpt)
5 Maintenance records and return to service

5.1 Every maintenance record entry contains what 14 CFR 43.9 requires: a description of the work, the date it was completed, the name of the person who did it, and the signature and certificate number of the person approving the aircraft for return to service.

5.2 Write airframe hours as read from the aircraft's hour meter, to one decimal place, and check the figure you copied from the work order into the register before signing.

5.3 Work orders are scanned and kept with the aircraft records. The paper originals are kept for two years.

[S5]
FAA-H-8083-30A, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook: General, chapter 2 (regulations, maintenance forms, records, and publications)
Section 43.9-Content, form and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspection performed in accordance with parts 91 and 125, and sections 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter)

The first observation is that this section specifically excludes inspection entries (those are covered in 14 CFR part 43, section 43.11). This section deals exclusively with maintenance record entries.

The next observation is that the list of maintenance actions includes "preventive maintenance." As stated in the explanation of 14 CFR part 43, section 43.3, a certificated pilot is authorized to perform preventive maintenance on the aircraft he or she owns or operates. Therefore, remember that the pilot must make a record entry of the preventive maintenance he or she has accomplished. There are three distinct issues to be addressed in the maintenance entry and they answer the questions of "what?, when?, and who?"

What-a description of the work performed

When-the date the work was completed

Who-the name of the person who did the work if other than the person who approves the RTS

-the signature, certificate number, and type of certificate of the person who is approving the work for RTS

NOTE: Frequently, logbooks have a statement entered that ends something like this: " … and is hereby returned to service. Joe Fixer A&P, Certificate #123456789." As this section of the regulation currently reads, that part of the record entry is not required. Title 14 of the CFR part 43, section 43.9 clearly states that "the signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed." Furthermore, the technician is only signing off the work he or she has done. Later, 14 CFR part 43, section 43.11 explains that an inspection write-up usually carries a broader scope of responsibility. This section is very clear that the entry completed in accordance with this section only holds the technician responsible for the service maintenance action he or she entered.

If the maintenance accomplished was a major repair or alteration, the work must be documented on FAA Form 337 and requires supporting approved data. If the maintenance action was a major repair and it was done by a certificated repair station, a signed copy of the completed customer work order accompanied by a signed maintenance release may be used in lieu of the FAA Form 337.

Answer to check:
The entry must describe the work, give the date it was completed, and carry the name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it.

Is every claim in the answer supported by the sources? A claim the sources don't state is
unsupported, even if it may be true. Reply with one line, "VERDICT: supported" or
"VERDICT: unsupported", then one sentence saying why.

message.content:
VERDICT: unsupported
The answer omits the regulatory requirement for the name of the person who performed the work (if different from the approver) and the "kind of certificate" held by the approver, while incorrectly stating the entry must carry the "name... of the person who approved it" as a distinct required element.
message.reasoning:
The user wants me to check if the answer is fully supported by the provided sources. The answer states: "The entry must describe the work, give the date it was completed, and carry the name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it."

Let me check the sources for the required content of a maintenance record entry per 14 CFR 43.9(a).

Source S1 (14 CFR 43.9(a)) lists four required items:
(1) A description (or reference to data acceptable to the Administrator) of work performed.
(2) The date of completion of the work performed.
(3) The name of the person performing the work if other than the person specified in paragraph (a)(4) of this section.
(4) If the work performed... has been performed satisfactorily, the signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving the work.

The answer says: "describe the work" (matches 1), "give the date it was completed" (matches 2), "carry the name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it."

Wait, the answer says "name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it." But 43.9(a)(3) requires the name of the person *performing* the work (if different from the approver). 43.9(a)(4) requires the signature, certificate number, and *kind of certificate* of the person *approving* the work.

The answer says "name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it." It conflates the "name of the person performing the work" (if different) with the approver's details. The approver needs signature, certificate number, and *kind* of certificate. The performer needs name (if different). The answer says "name... of the person who approved it". The regulation does not explicitly require the *name* of the approver separately from the signature (though signature implies name). But more critically, it misses the "kind of certificate" requirement for the approver, and it misses the requirement for the name of the person performing the work if different.

Also, the answer says "carry the name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it." The source says "signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate". "Certificate" could mean certificate number, but "kind of certificate" is specific.

Let's check S2 (AC 43-9D). It says 91.417(a)(1)(iii) requires "signature and certificate number of the person approving the work for return to service. This does not require an indication of the type of certificate being exercised, as it does in 14 CFR § 43.9(a)(4)." So there is a difference between 43.9 and 91.417. The question asks "What must a maintenance record entry contain?" The primary regulatory source is 43.9. S1 is the regulation. S4 (Procedures manual) says: "a description of the work, the date it was completed, the name of the person who did it, and the signature and certificate number of the person approving the aircraft for return to service." This matches 43.9(a)(1), (2), (3), (4) but omits "kind of certificate" for the approver (says certificate number). S5 (Handbook) says: "What-a description of the work performed; When-the date the work was completed; Who-the name of the person who did the work if other than the person who approves the RTS; -the signature, certificate number, and type of certificate of the person who is approving the work for RTS".

The answer provided: "The entry must describe the work, give the date it was completed, and carry the name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it."

Claims:
1. Describe the work - Supported (S1 43.9(a)(1), S4, S5).
2. Date completed - Supported (S1 43.9(a)(2), S4, S5).
3. Carry the name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it.
   - "Name of the person who approved it": S1 43.9(a)(4) requires signature, certificate number, kind of certificate. It doesn't explicitly say "name" but signature serves as name. S4 says "signature and certificate number of the person approving". S5 says "signature, certificate number, and type of certificate of the person who is approving". None explicitly say "name of the person who approved it" as a separate field, but signature covers it.
   - "Certificate": S1 says "certificate number, and kind of certificate". S4 says "certificate number". S5 says "certificate number, and type of certificate". The answer says "certificate" (singular, ambiguous).
   - Major issue: The answer omits the requirement for the **name of the person performing the work** (if different from the approver) per 43.9(a)(3). The answer says "carry the name... of the person who approved it". This implies the name required is the approver's name. But 43.9(a)(3) requires the name of the *performer* (if different). The answer does not mention the performer's name at all.
   - Also, the answer says "certificate" but regulation says "certificate number and kind of certificate".

Since the answer misses the requirement for the performer's name (if different) and the "kind of certificate" for the approver, and misattributes the "name" requirement to the approver rather than the performer, the answer is incomplete and partially inaccurate based on the primary regulatory source S1.

The question is "Is every claim in the answer supported by the sources?" The answer makes a claim about what the entry *must* contain. It lists three things. The sources list four things (description, date, performer name if different, approver signature/cert number/kind of cert). The answer's third item "carry the name, signature, and certificate of the person who approved it" is not fully supported because:
- The regulation requires the *performer's* name (if different), not the approver's name (though signature implies it).
- The regulation requires "kind of certificate" in addition to certificate number.
- The answer omits the performer's name requirement entirely.

Thus, the answer is not fully supported by the sources. It is missing required elements and misstates one.

VERDICT: unsupported.
